subject.title: [Feature]: [Feature Request] OpenClaw WebChat: Conversation Management & Multi-AI Collaboration

question: Should #27526 remain the canonical core tracker, and which remaining WebChat project-directory and multi-AI collaboration pieces belong in core versus plugin, ClawHub, or API-extension work?
rationale: Current main satisfies many session-management primitives, while the remaining project/committee workflow crosses UX, Gateway protocol, persisted state, and orchestration boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Keep Canonical And Split
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to define separate milestones for project/session metadata, directory navigation, and multi-agent collaboration semantics.

options.title: Narrow To Session UX
options.body: Limit near-term core work to existing session grouping, search, pin/archive/rename, and switching while leaving committee and project-tracking workflows out of scope for now.

options.title: Route Collaboration Out Of Core
options.body: Keep the session-directory work in core but direct committee, consensus, and multi-agent orchestration experiments to plugins or ClawHub until a smaller API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical And Split
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to define separate milestones for project/session metadata, directory navigation, and multi-agent collaboration semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already gave the canonical-tracker signal and are the clearest product-routing owner in the issue discussion.
